questions.question: _________, built by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in the 17th century, was the main residence of the Mughal Emperors for nearly 200 years.

• The Red Fort was created to serve as the abode of the Royal Mughal families and was named** Quila-E-Mubarak**.

• **Salimgarh Fort** was built in **1546** AD in Delhi on a former land of the** Yamuna River by Salim Shah Suri son of Sher Shah Suri**.

questions.question: GDP can be expressed in two different ways, nominal GDP and _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**real GDP.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Real gross domestic product (real GDP) is an** inflation-adjusted measure** that reflects the value of **all goods and services** produced by an economy in a given year (expressed in base-year prices).
 
• Real GDP tracks the** total value of goods and services **by calculating the quantities but using constant prices that are adjusted for inflation.
 
• **Nominal GDP** = Real GDP x GDP Deflator.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• GDP-gross domestic product; the **total value of all the goods and services** produced in a country in **one year**.
 
• GDP is important because it gives information about the size of the economy and how an economy is performing.
 
• Four types of GDP- **Real GDP, Nominal GDP, Actual GDP, and Potential GDP**.
 
• Nominal GDP-Nominal GDP is an **assessment of economic production** in an economy that includes current prices in its calculation.
 
• Potential GDP-In economics, potential output refers to the highest level of real gross domestic product that can be sustained over the long term.​

questions.question: In which part the Article 44 of the Constitution of India is mentioned as the provision for a uniform civil code for the citizens contained?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Part IV.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The source of the concept of Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) is the** Spanish Constitution** from which it came from the** Irish** Constitution.
 
• Part IV of the Constitution of India **(Article 36–51)** contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• Article 37 of the Indian Constitution States about the application of the Directive Principles.
 
• The DPSP is** not enforceable by law**; it is non-justiciable.
 
• DPSP consists of all the ideals which the State should follow and keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws for the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Important articles in ****Part IV**.

 
 
• Article 38 Constitution of India: State to secure a social order for the** promotion of the welfare of the people**.
 
• Article 39A Constitution of India: **Equal justice and free legal aid**.
 
• Article 40 Constitution of India: Organisation of **village panchayats**.
 
• Article 41 Constitution of India: **Right to work, to education** and to public assistance in certain cases.
 
• Article 42 Constitution of India: Provision for just and humane conditions of work and** maternity relief**.
 
• Article 43B Constitution of India: Promotion of cooperative Societies.
 
• Article 44 Constitution of India:** Uniform civil code for the citizens**.
 
• Article 46 Constitution of India: **Promotion** of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections.
 
• Article 48 Constitution of India: **Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry**.
 
• Article 48A Constitution of India**: Protection and improvement of environment** and safeguarding of forests and wildlife.
 
• Article 49 Constitution of India: Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Part III**- Articles **12 to 35** contained in Part III of the Constitution deal with** Fundamental Rights**.
 
• **Part II**- Citizenship of India constitutional provisions. **Citizenship **in India is governed by** Articles 5 – 11 (Part II**) of the Constitution.
 
 
• The Citizenship Act, of 1955 is the legislation dealing with citizenship.
 
 
 
• **Part VI **(Article **152 to Article 237**)- The executive power of the State shall be vested in the** Governor **and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with this Constitution.

questions.question: Kabini is an important tributary of the river _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cauvery.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The River Cauvery** originates at** Talakaveri in the Coorg District of Karnataka** in the** Brahmagiri Range** of hills in the Western ghats at an elevation of 1341 m.
 
• The Cauvery basin is bounded by the **Tungabhadra sub-basin of the Krishna basin on the Northern side and the Palar basin** on the Southern side.
 
• Cauvery basin extends over an area of **81155 sq, km, **which is nearly** 2.7%** of the total geographical area of the country.
 
• Kaveri River widens as many rivers join her in the course of her journey, **Shimsha, Hemavati, Kabini, Arkavathy, Honnuhole, Bhavani, Lokapavani, Amaravati and Noyil** are the tributaries of river Cauvery.
 
• The total length of the Kaveri river from the origin to its outfall into the** Bay of Bengal** is **805 Kms**.
 
• Kaveri river, also known as the** Ponni river**, is famous as the **Ganga of the South**. Source (the Godavari is Dakshin Ganga.
 
• Kaveri river finally merges into the** Bay of Bengal** to the **South of Cuddalore**, Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Krishna river**-The river Krishna finds its mention in Puranas as river Krsnavena, and river Kanhaperna in the Jatakas stories.

 
 
• Krishna river is the 2nd largest river in peninsular India,1st being the Godavari river.
 
• River Krishna originates in the Western ghats at the Jor village of Maharashtra near Mahabaleshwar about 64 km from the Arabian Sea.
 
• Krishna river starts from Maharashtra and then flows through Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh it merges into the Bay of Bengal.​
 
 
 
• **Godavari river**- Godavari is the** largest of the peninsular rivers** of India and the** third largest** river in India.
 
 
• Also known as **Dakshin Ganga **or **Vridha Ganga**.
 
• ​Drains about 10% of India’s total geographical area.
 
• Source– Godavari rises near **Thriambak Hills** in the **Nasik district **of **Maharashtra state**, at an elevation of 1,067 m in the Western Ghats.
 
• The Godavari flows for about 1,465 km., in a southeast direction, and merges into the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Mahi river**-The Mahi basin lies in the states of** Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat**.
 
 
• Originates from the northern slopes of Vindhyas at an altitude of 500 m near **village Bhopawar, Sardarpur tehsil in Dhar** district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It drains into the Arabian Sea through the** Gulf of Khambhat**.

questions.question: In which state was the Forest Martyrs' Memorial inaugurated in November 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Forest martyrs memorial was inaugurated in **Nagaravanam, Rajamahedravaram city, Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It was built to commemorate **22 forest martyrs** who laid their lives for the **protection of the forest and wildlife**.
 
• In their memory, an audio song and a video song were released in the program.
 
• **National Forest Martyrs Day** is marked and observed every year on **September 11**.

questions.question: Queen Victoria's Proclamation declared that thereafter India would be governed by and in the name of the British Monarch through a Secretary of State on ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 November 1858.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Queen Victoria's Proclamation of** 1 November 1858 **declared that thereafter India would be governed by and in the name of the** British Monarch through a Secretary of State**.
 
• The East India Company's rule in India came to an end.
 
• The** Act of 1858** was known as the Act for the better Government of India.
 
• The Act of 1858 was given royal assent on **2nd August 1858** but was commenced o **1st November 1858**.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The act of 1858 was related to the **power transfer** from the East India Company to the** British crown**.
 
• The act abolished the dual government of the **Pitts India act**.
 
• The act also abolished the** doctrine of lapse**.
 
• The secretary of state for India was** Lord Stanely** and the first Governor general and viceroy of India was** Lord canning**.

questions.question: The Buddhist Vihara at Sanchi is also known as the 'Great Stupa'. It is one of the most famous Buddhist monuments in India, located at Sanchi town in ________ district.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Raisen.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sachi Stupa.**

 
 
• Stupa at Sanchi is a **world heritage site**. 
 
• It was built by **Ashoka** in the** 3rd century** BCE. 
 
• It is the most prominent and the oldest and is believed to have Buddha’s relics.
 
• Along with other relatively small stupas, there are three main stupas at Sanchi.
 
• The Great Stupa and Sanchi’s other Buddhist monuments were collectively designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1989.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raisen**.

 
 
• Raisen District is a district of** Madhya Pradesh** state of India.
 
• Bhopal State of independent India came into being, and Raisen was declared a separate district on 5 May 1950.
 
• Raisen District has many tourist places like **Sanchi:- World heritage, 46 km from Bhopal** and 32 km from Vidisha, Bhojpur.
 
• The** Bhojpur temple** houses one of the largest Shiva lingams in India.
 
 
 
• **Jabalpur.**
 
 
• Jabalpur district is a district of** Madhya Pradesh **state in central India.
 
• Jabalpur district is located in the **Mahakoshal region of Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• famous for its **Marble Rocks and scenic charms.**
 
 
 
• **​Purnia****.**
 
 
• Purnia District is one of the thirty-eight districts of the Indian state of Bihar.​
 
• Purnia is part of the Mithila region,Mithila first gained prominence after it was settled by Indo-Aryan peoples.
